claims.text: The initial material is zirconium-alloy cladding coated with pure elemental chromium.
A few weight percent aluminum should be introduced into the chromium coating during deposition.
Aluminum doping will cause a fine-scale, stable Al2O3 phase to form within the chromium matrix or at its interface with zirconium.
The Al2O3 phase will act as a barrier to interdiffusion between chromium and zirconium.
Aluminum facilitates in-situ Al2O3 formation during high-temperature oxidation of the chromium coating.
The resulting alumina layer is sufficiently chemically inert to reduce Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Alumina formation will improve the oxidation resistance of the coating.
Alumina formation will preserve coating integrity in both subcritical-water and high-temperature-steam service.
Relative to pure Cr, Al-doped Cr will have a lower oxidation rate.
Relative to pure Cr, Al-doped Cr will have significantly diminished Cr-Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Relative to pure Cr, Al-doped Cr will have improved long-term coating durability and integrity under both normal and accident conditions.
The proposed benefit is applicable to subcritical-water exposure at approximately 360 degrees Celsius.
The proposed benefit is applicable to high-temperature steam exposure up to approximately 1200 degrees Celsius.
The proposed benefit persists over exposure times typical of reactor operation and accident transients.
The optimal aluminum concentration is not established.
The long-term stability of the Al-doped coating under neutron irradiation is not established.
The kinetics of alumina-scale formation under dynamic reactor conditions are not established.
